answer: In a bridge inspection market, agents can whisper praise for aliases, so reward signed readings rather than endorsements. Register each physical probe once and let a public lottery choose which span it samples. An umber paint mark is not proof: each reading must carry the probe signature and a fresh challenge nonce. The ledger pays once per assigned reading. To collect more, a fraudster must enroll real probes or compromise their keys; dishonest enrollment remains a weakness.
